title: Lumentum CEO warns laser shortage could outlast the AI chip crunch
key_facts: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston said at the RAISE Summit in Paris on 8 July that the shortage of indium phosphide, the material for lasers in AI data centre optical transceivers, could become more acute than the memory chip shortage.
On Lumentum's May earnings call he said demand for EML and pump lasers exceeds supply by more than 30%.
Nvidia put $2 billion into Lumentum in March and the same amount into Coherent, tied to future capacity access and purchase commitments, per Yahoo Finance coverage cited by the article.
The article says Lumentum expects to sell out its entire 2028 production capacity within the next two quarters.

China added indium phosphide to its export control list in February 2025; the article says Beijing controls about 70% of global refined indium and Chinese indium exports fell about 72% year on year by late 2025.
Lumentum's guidance suggests the laser imbalance will not ease between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027, with capacity added in phases from 2026 to 2028.
The article argues the laser shortage could limit how fast data centres can network their GPUs, even if they have enough chips.
quote_evidence: The shortage of indium phosphide, I think, will become even more acute than what we see from the memory guys.
On Lumentum's May earnings call, Hurlston put a number on it: demand for EML and pump lasers now exceeds supply by more than 30%.
Between the two of us, I don't think we can service the demand that Nvidia and others are now putting on us.
why_it_matters_hint: A shortage of laser parts could limit how quickly AI data centres can link their chips, but this is one executive's view of his own market.
event_date: 8 July (remarks at RAISE Summit, Paris); May earnings call; the article gives no year, context points to 2026
notes: OLDER NEWS RE-DATED: the pool date is 2 Oct 2026 but the article's own events are the 8 July conference remarks and the May earnings call. Year not stated in the text; inferred as 2026 from the surrounding dates (March investment, fiscal 2026/2027 guidance). Claims are the CEO's own and one outlet's reading; the article cites TechTimes, LEDinside and mlq.ai second-hand.
